subject: chemistry
title: Atomic Structure Adventure 2: Electron configuration and orbitals
welcome_lead: Today you'll fill s, p, d orbitals — and write electron configurations.
meta_desc: IBDP Chemistry — electron configuration, sub-shells s/p/d, Aufbau, Hund's rule, ionisation energies.
final_note: You learned electrons fill shells via Aufbau (1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p), each sub-shell holds 2/6/10, and IE evidence supports this.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Each shell n splits into sub-shells s, p, d, f:

- n=1: 1s (2 e⁻)
- n=2: 2s + 2p (2 + 6 = 8 e⁻)
- n=3: 3s + 3p + 3d (2 + 6 + 10 = 18 e⁻)
- n=4: 4s + 4p + 4d + 4f (32 e⁻)

Each orbital holds max 2 electrons with opposite spin (Pauli).

Aufbau filling order (energy-based):

1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p 5s 4d 5p 6s 4f 5d 6p ...

Examples:
- Na (Z=11): 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s¹
- Ca (Z=20): 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s²
- Fe (Z=26): 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶ 4s² (often written this way)

Exceptions: Cr [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹ and Cu [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ — stable half/full d.

First IE: M(g) → M⁺(g) + e⁻.

Across period: IE generally rises (more protons, same shell).

Down group: IE falls (more shells, shielding).

Successive IE plots show jumps when moving to inner shells — directly evidencing shell structure.

Nature of science: IE data confirmed quantum mechanical orbital model.
